hero.description: In a study of some 66,000 US households from 1991–96 (Barber & Odean, 2000), the fifth that traded most earned about 7 percentage points a year less, after costs, than the fifth that traded least. PivoxQuant mirrors your own trading pattern back to you and makes you pause once, right before you trade. No scores, no stock picks. Observational data only, not a directive to act.
hero.disclaimer: Not investment advice. Informational research only. Past performance does not guarantee future results.

steps.heading: Upload. Pause. Record. Look back.
steps.deck: Your own record is the only material, and all the tool does is show it back to you later.
steps.s1body: You start by uploading what you already hold. Capture your broker app's holdings screen and the ticker, quantity and average cost are read in your browser; you check each row before it is saved. If a capture does not fit, enter holdings one at a time.
steps.s1limit: It does not link to your account.
steps.s2body: Seven questions before you hit buy. Why now, what would prove you wrong, whether you can afford to lose this. The time it takes to write the answers is the only friction.
steps.s2limit: It does not pick stocks for you.
steps.s3body: What you bought and what you almost bought sit in the same place. Upload a broker file or a fill notification and the numbers are filled in; you write only why. Holding period, turnover, concentration, averaging down, how you close winners and losers — five habits computed straight from that record.
steps.s4body: The investor you declared at onboarding, next to the investor your last 30 days of trades describe. Where those two diverge, across several axes, is the whole of this tool.
steps.s4limit: It does not say which one is right.
steps.pauseTitle: The trades you did not make count too
steps.pauseBody: When you record a buy and there is a recent pause on the same ticker, the two are linked — on by default, and you can untick it. The record page counts how your pauses ended (went ahead, cancelled, open) and, of the cancelled ones, how many you never bought and how many you bought anyway. It does not say which was better.
steps.notifyBody: If one sector passes 30% of your holdings at cost, you get an in-app alert. Turn it on in Settings and a PDF of last month's record arrives by email early each month. The weekly pulse is a short form on the record page where you write down your own mood and confidence for the week.

faq.deck: What people ask most before starting the beta.
faq.heading: Before you begin.
faq.q1: Is this the same as investment advisory?
faq.a1: No. It falls outside licensed investment advisory under Article 6 of the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act. PivoxQuant is an informational research tool that reflects back the record and holdings you entered yourself. It does not pick securities, score them, or tell you to buy or sell. Every decision remains yours.
faq.q2: What do you do with my trade data — what does the mirror “observe”?
faq.a2: It places two things side by side: what you said about your own habits in the five onboarding questions, and the behaviour observed in your last 30 days of trades. Nine axes — average holding period, turnover, sector spread and so on — are computed from your own record; no new judgement is manufactured. Raw trade data is stored encrypted and is never used for advertising or sold onward. You can download it from Settings as JSON or CSV at any time, and on account deletion it is fully erased within 30 days.
faq.q3: Do the declared and observed sides change over time?
faq.a3: The observed side is recomputed from your last 30 days of trades. What you declared stays put until you answer the five questions again — the point of the mirror is to show where the two diverge, not to give you a type or pick one for you.
faq.q4: What do I actually do here?
faq.a4: Four things. Upload what you already hold, pause before you buy and leave your reasoning in seven questions (Pre-Trade), record what you bought and sold with the reason (Portfolio · Journal), and weeks later look at the you those records describe (Mirror). Your own record is the only material.
faq.q5: Do you have access to my brokerage account?
faq.a5: No — and there is nothing to connect. Automatic brokerage linking is not offered, and no API keys or account credentials are collected. Holdings are uploaded from a capture of your broker app's holdings screen (read in your browser; the image is never sent to the server) or entered one at a time, and are registered as soon as you check and save them. Fills can be entered by hand, uploaded from a trade-history file, a fill-screen capture or fill-notification text, or sent by your own automation tool with an import token issued in Settings. On every path the server never touches your brokerage, and a fill that arrives by file, capture or notification is not recorded until you write why and approve it.
faq.a6: Everything is free during the closed beta. Paid plans are not active, and you will be told in advance if that changes.
faq.q7: Do I have to type in every trade by hand?
faq.a7: Not the numbers. There are four paths. ① Download your trade history from your broker app as CSV/Excel/PDF (up to 2MB) and upload it — column names are matched automatically (scanned PDFs without text excluded). ② Upload a capture of a major broker's fill-history screen and the text is read in your browser and laid out as fill rows. The image is never sent to the server — only the rows it read. Cells it is not sure of stay blank for you to fill in. ③ Copy a fill notification and paste it; ticker, quantity, price and time are read from it. On Android you can send it straight from the share sheet. ④ Issue an import token in Settings and let your own automation forward fill notifications as they arrive: on Android an app like MacroDroid forwards the notification, on iPhone a Shortcuts automation can forward the broker's fill SMS — only with brokers that still send fills by text message. On every path the fill waits in your inbox until you write one line on why and approve it, and only then is it recorded. The original file is discarded after parsing; next to each fill only one line of the source text is kept, with account numbers masked.

whatIsService.a: PivoxQuant is an informational service that organizes the investment record you enter yourself and reflects it back to you. It is not investment advice and does not recommend specific securities or provide advice tailored to any individual. All information on the platform is for reference only. Investment decisions and their outcomes are entirely the responsibility of the user.

dataSource.q: Where does the data come from?
dataSource.a: Company, financial, and disclosure data are sourced exclusively from officially licensed providers (Korea Investment & Securities API, SEC EDGAR, KRX/DART official public data, etc.). Unofficial scraping is not used. Holding amounts are calculated from the average cost you entered; market prices are not displayed.

pricing.a: Everything is free during the closed beta. Paid plans are not active, and you will be told in advance if that changes.

howToLogin.a: You can sign in with your Google or Kakao account. Separate email/password registration is not offered. If sign-in fails, try updating your browser to the latest version or disable private/incognito mode, then try again.

deleteAccount.q: How do I delete my account?
deleteAccount.a: Settings → Danger zone → Delete account. By default the request starts a 30-day grace period: you are signed out and sign-in is blocked, and the confirmation email carries a link to cancel. After 30 days every record is permanently purged (PIPA §21). The same dialog also offers an immediate, irreversible deletion. If you run into a problem, contact us via the 1:1 inquiry form.

pwa.q: Can I install PivoxQuant as an app? (PWA)
pwa.a: PivoxQuant is a Progressive Web App (PWA). On mobile or desktop browsers, use the 'Add to Home Screen' or 'Install' option to install it like a native app. Once installed, it runs full-screen for a faster experience.

staleData.q: The data or screen looks outdated.
staleData.a: Refreshing your browser will reload the latest records. If you have the PWA installed, try fully closing and reopening the app.

contact.a: After signing in, you can submit a question about your account or how to use the platform through the 1:1 inquiry form. Your submitted inquiries and responses are available in 'My Inquiries'.

importTokens.guideIntro: When your broker sends a 'filled' notification, your phone forwards that text to PivoxQuant for you. Fills land on the pending list on the Journal page without typing each one; approve them with your reason and they are recorded. The token is the key that proves the phone is sending for your account.
importTokens.guideNeedAndroid: Android — the MacroDroid app (Play Store, free). It reads your broker app's fill push or KakaoTalk message as is.
importTokens.guideNeedIos: iPhone — the built-in Shortcuts app. Fill notices must arrive by text message (SMS); Shortcuts cannot read other apps' push or KakaoTalk messages. If your broker has no SMS notice, use screenshot or paste import on the Journal page instead.
importTokens.guideStep1: ① Issue a token below. Name it after the device (e.g. Galaxy MacroDroid).
importTokens.guideStep2: ② Copy the token shown right after issuing. It cannot be shown again once you close it.
importTokens.guideStep3: ③ Follow the phone setup shown on the same screen to create one 'fill notification → send to PivoxQuant' rule in MacroDroid or Shortcuts. It takes about five minutes.
importTokens.guideStep4: ④ From the next fill on, it appears on the pending list at the top of the Journal page. Approve it with your reason to record it, or reject what you don't need.
importTokens.guideNote1: The token can only place fills on the pending list. It never touches your brokerage account or orders.
importTokens.guideNote2: If you change phones or think the token leaked, revoke it in the list below and issue a new one.
importTokens.setupKicker: Phone setup — copy and paste these three values
importTokens.headerLabel: Header — name Authorization, value this line
importTokens.android1: 1. Install and open MacroDroid, then tap 'Add Macro'.
importTokens.android2: 2. Trigger → 'Notifications' → 'Notification Received'. Pick your broker app (KakaoTalk if notices come as KakaoTalk messages) and add '체결' as the text condition.
importTokens.android4: 4. Method POST; paste the 'Address to send to' into the URL field.
importTokens.android5: 5. Add a header: name Authorization, value the 'Bearer …' line above, pasted as is.
importTokens.android6: 6. Content type application/json; body {"text":"[notification]"}. [notification] is the MacroDroid variable that becomes the received notification text.
importTokens.android7: 7. Save, then allow MacroDroid 'Notification access' in the phone settings. Exempting it from battery optimisation keeps it from missing notices.
importTokens.ios1: 1. In your broker app (or via its support line), switch fill notices to text message (SMS).
importTokens.ios2: 2. Shortcuts → Automation → New Automation → 'Message'. Set 'Message contains' to '체결' and choose 'Run Immediately'.
importTokens.ios3: 3. Add action → 'Get Contents of URL'. Paste the 'Address to send to' as the URL.
importTokens.ios4: 4. Change Method to POST and add a header: key Authorization, value the 'Bearer …' line above.
importTokens.ios5: 5. Request Body JSON → Add new field (Text): key text, value the 'Shortcut Input' variable (the received message).
importTokens.test1: When the next fill notice arrives, look at the pending list at the top of the Journal page. The 'Last used' time in the token list below also changes.
importTokens.test2: Nothing arrived? Check that the notice text contains '체결', that the header value starts with 'Bearer ', and that MacroDroid's notification access is on.

monthlyReport.what: On the 1st of each month at 08:30 KST, we email a PDF of the fills and pauses you recorded over the last 30 days. If you recorded nothing in that period, nothing is sent.
monthlyReport.contents: What it holds: fills you recorded · acquiring more of a position you already had · round trips closed in the period · concentration at average cost · how each pause ended. No quotes and no scores, and the reasons you wrote in a pause are not copied in.
monthlyReport.gateCell: Monthly mirror report · email, in the table above
monthlyReport.willSend: All three are on. The next send is on {date}.
monthlyReport.wontSend: With the current settings nothing will be sent. Turn on what is off and it starts from the next 1st.
monthlyReport.downloadNote: The same PDF as the email, built for the last 30 days as of now.
monthlyReport.empty: No fills or pauses were recorded in the last 30 days, so there is no report to build yet.
monthlyReport.tooMany: Please try again in a moment. Reports can be built 5 times a minute.
monthlyReport.failed: The report could not be built. Please try again in a moment.
